docs/how-it-works.md:12:4. **Save pi thread state** ([`src/push.ts`](../src/push.ts)). This step has `if: always()`. It saves the working tree one more time, and pushes the thread if the run did not push all of it, for example after a cancellation, a timeout, or a crash.
docs/how-it-works.md:24:7. **Work** ([`src/conversation.ts`](../src/conversation.ts)). While pi works, pi-action adds new `@pi` comments to the conversation, and saves the working tree and pushes the thread after each model response and tool result. At `timeout`, pi-action stops pi and reports the timeout.
docs/threads.md:23:- In the `Save pi thread state` step of the action, which has `if: always()`. This step pushes commits that the main step did not push, for example after a crash or a timeout. It also saves the working tree one more time (see [Working-tree continuity](#working-tree-continuity)).
docs/threads.md:50:pi-action saves a **snapshot** of the working tree after each model response and tool result, at the end of the run, and in the `Save pi thread state` step. It saves a snapshot only when the files changed since the last snapshot. A snapshot contains:
CONTRIBUTING.md:105:| [`src/push.ts`](src/push.ts) | The `if: always()` step that saves the working tree and pushes thread state that the run did not push |
CONTRIBUTING.md:106:| [`src/worktree.ts`](src/worktree.ts) | `WorktreeContinuity`: saves the working tree at turn boundaries, points the conversation at each snapshot (the `pi-action.worktree` document), and restores it at the start of a run |
